items.body: Day three of our celebration of Miles Davis at 100. See day one and two here. By Stef Gijssels The year 1970 marked an extraordinary turning point in Miles Davis’s career and artistic evolution. He transformed himself from a jazz musician into a figure with the presence — and attitude — of a rock star. His music became increasingly exploratory and electric: wah-wah trumpet effects, fractured and layered textures, electric piano, electric bass, and organ all became central to his sound. Equally important were the relentless rhythms, the unrestrained improvisations, and the trance-like length and density of the performances. It represented a complete break from conventional jazz harmony, moving instead toward something more primal, ritualistic, and less bound by eclectic convention. While many jazz purists rejected this new direction, rock audiences embraced it enthusiastically. He performed with an exceptional list of musicians in this year, all of which individually became famous in their own right, and some of them created the most popular fusion bands of the seventies and eighties: the John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra, Chick Corea's Return to Forever, and Joe Zawinul and Wayne Shorter's Weather Report. Miles Davis opened the door to something else completely. The Cellar Door Sessions 1970 (Columbia, 2005) My preferred album by Miles Davis is without a doubt " Bitches Brew ", followed by " In A Silent Way ", discussed before. From the same period are a few other excellent albums, including this compilation released in 2005 only. It was recorded live over a few nights in December 1970 at The Cellar Door , a club in Washington DC. The six-CD box comprises six of the ten recorded tracks, some of which have already officially been released as part of " Live-Evil ". With its six hours of music, this album is guaranteed to give you an overdose of the Miles of that period: lengthy tracks, improvisations, brutal yet quality interplay, some moments of fun even. You get five different versions of " Directions " (also called " Call It Anything " on the triple vinyl of the Isle of Wight Rock Festival of 1970) and " What I Say" (on Live-Evil) , four versions of " Honky Tonk ", also called " Funky Tonk " on " Live-Evil", and two versions of " It's About That Time" ( from "In A Silent Way"). Some parts of the improvisation and " Inamorata ", were also used on "Live-Evil " and called " Inamorata and Narration by Conrad Roberts ". So much for the factoids, but it's about the music and that is absolutely stellar, as is the quality of the recording. Some call this "fusion" or "jazz rock" but those are truly deceptive classifications for this period in Davis's career. Yes, there is a strong and solid rhythm section, yet the themes and the improvisation are as open as jazz can be, with solid interplay for sure, but still far away from the soulless over-polished technical pyrotechnics of so much of fusion music. The pieces are long, and actually some performances move from one piece into the next without a break, it's a continuous never-ending party of great music, raw at times, offering the level of spontaneous creation that cannot happen without some raw or noisy overall sound. The fun part of the many versions is that it allows you to compare the freedom that the musicians have in their performances, and the difference in their collective rendition of the same music. The band are Miles Davis on trumpet, Gary Bartz on saxes, Keith Jarrett on electric piano and organ, Michael Henderson on electric bass, Jack DeJohnette on drums, Airo Moreira on percussion (except disc one), and with John McLaughlin joining on guitar for disc 5 & 6 (recorded on December 19, 1970). A stellar band at the height of its skills, and music that is relatively unique in its sound and quality. It's a lot to digest, a huge meal of exquisite ingredients. A Tribute To Jack Johnson (Columbia, 1970) This album was recorded right after " Bitches Brew ", in April 1970, and was conceived as a soundtrack for a documentary by Bill Cayton about the heavyweight world champion boxer Jack Johnson . It contains two lengthy pieces, performed by two different line-ups: Right Off " has Miles Davis on trumpet, Steve Grossman on saxophone, John McLaughlin on guitar, Herbie Hancock on organ, Michael Henderson on bass, and Billy Cobham on drums, and " Yesternow " has Miles Davis on trumpet, John McLaughlin and Sonny Sharock on guitar, Bennie Maupin on bass clarinet, Chick Corea on electric piano, Dave Holland on bass, and Jack DeJohnette on drums. The two tracks are heavily post-produced, a kind of collage by producer Teo Macero, whose "cut and paste" approach of different jam sections and solos are brought to a new level. The collage is not always really audible although some radical rhythm changes in the pieces indicate some artificial interventions. While waiting for Miles to arrive, McLaughlin starts the first track by a rock-ish guitar vamp, and is joined by Cobham and Henderson on bass and drums. Apparently Herbie Hancock happened to be around the studio that day, so he joined too. It was not yet meant to be recorded, yet it was. The trumpet just joins after a few minutes and the piece gets its full voice. As the Miles Davis website explains: "“ Right Off” (the opposite of the catchphrase of the day, “right on”) travels a long path, including a moment (18:44) when McLaughlin repeatedly hammers a riff from Sly Stone’s “Sing A Simple Song”, and into a series of ringing power chords, a searing saxophone solo, and further guitar ribaldry. “Yesternow” (the very title balancing past and present) opens with a more spaced-out feel, includes a snippet of “Shhh/Peaceful” from In A Silent Way (Miles literally sampling himself!) " Both tracks are excellent, post-produced, collaged or not. The music is hypnotic as is most of Davis's work of that period, yet it adds the specific political message of civil rights in the USA. Even if this theme is omnipresent in his work implicitly, here it becomes a real message. The album ends with the voice of Brock Peters, speaking on behalf of Jack Johnson in the documentary. “ I’m Jack Johnson, heavyweight champion of the world! I’m black! They never let me forget it. I’m black all right. I’ll never let them forget it. ” Miles Davis writes in the liner notes: “ Johnson portrayed Freedom… the more they hated him, the more money he made, the more women he got and the more wine he drank. ” Freedom is to be liberated from the shackles of preconceived notions, of conventions, of racist history. This music is Freedom. Live At Fillmore (Columbia, 1970) Recorded live at the Filmore in June 1970, this album takes advantage of the success of " In A Silent Way " and " Bitches Brew ". The show contains much of the material of both albums, again with a great band of Chick Corea and Keith Jarrett on electric keyboards, Steve Grossman on saxophones and flute, Dave Holland on bass, Jack DeJohnette on drums, Airto Moreira on percussion. The music is edited to allow for all major compositions to be represented on this double vinyl. Tracks move almost seamlessly into one another. At the same time, you never know about what was edited: " Miles was in the habit of kicking off tunes before the previous one had ended, overlapping in into another, making it difficult to pull out discreet performances ", and even stronger, making the band follow suit instantly. The sound quality is excellent, and fans of the electric Miles should definitely check it out. Live-Evil (Columbia, 1971) Recorded between February and December 1970, " Live-Evil" ends the phenomenal year of Miles psychedelic jazz style. The entire cast of musicians is actually rarely a complete band, but an ensemble that changes on every track. Miles Davis on trumpet, Gary Bartz, Steve Grossman, Wayne Shorter on sax, John McLaughlin on electric guitar, Keith Jarrett on organ, Herbie Hancock, Chick Corea and Joe Zawinul on electric piano, Michael Henderson, Dave Holland and Ron Carter on bass, Billy Cobham, Jack DeJohnette and Hermeto Pascoal on drums and vocals, Airto Moreira and Khalil Balakrishna on electric sitar. The label describes the album appropriately: " it bulges at the seams in its effort to contain all Miles was up to the year before—the crazy diversity of experiences in 1970. (The sounds) ranged from rock-band abandon spilling off of small club stages, to ambient jams and mood pieces crafted in the recording studio. He was working a wider sonic mix than ever—wah-wah trumpet (within the album’s first minute!) and Indian sitar, electric guitar and electronic keyboards, whistling and vocalizing and shouts, spoken poetry and the “speaking” of the Brazilian cuíca all over. The music is a crazy psychedelic mix—not jazz or rock or funk. Not this or that. Willfully kaleidoscopic and boldly futuristic ." It is a strange album, with many different styles and unexpected twists and turns. It is not a "live" album as its title might suggest, but rather an collection of musical pieces of which some were recorded live. The core of the album is made of three very long tracks " What I Say " (phenomenal!), " Funky Tonk ", and " Inamorata ", tied together with shorter and more subdued interludes. The album ends with a poem by Conrad Roberts "Inamorato Mission: music, masculinity Master of the art: music Who is this music that which description may never justify? Can the ocean be described? Fathomless music Body of all that is Live ever lastingly Men, initiate Inamorato, your music art tomorrow's unknown known life I love tomorrow" Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._cn_summary: 1970年是Miles Davis艺术生涯的重要转折点，标志着他从传统爵士向电气化、实验性方向的彻底转型。文章详细阐述了他引入哇音吉他、电钢琴、电贝司等电子元素，配合即兴演奏的高密度节奏结构，形成所谓的融合爵士雏形。评论指出，当年的合作音乐人日后均成为各自领域的标志性人物，包括Mahavishnu Orchestra、Return to Forever及Weather Report的创始成员。《The Cellar Door Sessions 1970》收录长达六小时的现场录音，涵盖多首曲目的不同版本，展现了这一时期音乐的开放性与即兴能量。评论特别强调，尽管被归类为融合或爵士摇滚，但Miles的音乐本质上保持着爵士的即兴精神，与后来商业化的融合风格存在本质差异。此类跨越音乐类型界限、具备实验精神的作品，与用户偏好高度吻合。

items.excerpt: soak vol 2 unfolds like a damaged transmission from somewhere intimate and unplaceable—32 fractured, emotional, and strangely beautiful pieces stitched together from the outer edges of contemporary electronic sound. An international community focused on contemporary sound soak vol 2 by soak   Angular and granular electronica with some minor guitarica. There is probably no dancing and definitely no sleeping, this is all art—so rejoice! 32 very strange episodes, plenty to baffle the listener.
items.body: soak vol 2 unfolds like a damaged transmission from somewhere intimate and unplaceable—32 fractured, emotional, and strangely beautiful pieces stitched together from the outer edges of contemporary electronic sound. An international community focused on contemporary sound soak vol 2 by soak   Angular and granular electronica with some minor guitarica. There is probably no dancing and definitely no sleeping, this is all art—so rejoice! 32 very strange episodes, plenty to baffle the listener. Soak (the record label) is based in Petropavl, Kazakhstan. Soak 2 is a second compilation album by that label, an international community focused on contemporary sound as a means of emotional liberation & self-inquiry, featuring various kinds of music, ranging from lamebient & downtempo to quirky sound-design, raw sonic intimacy & processed emo, whatever that may be. “This is something we are proud to share, aiming at fostering a sense of unity, artistic freedom & love.“ The project was gathered and meticulously curated throughout 2025. “We hadn’t planned it to turn out that long, 32 tracks crept up like an uncontrolled desire of getting tattooed over and over again. As a result, ‘soak body’ is etched with a (s)extensive selection of self-recognition-evoking music by sound producers & musicians across the globe. Raw or refined, recorded live, carefully produced, (un)processed or playfully generated, the diversity of sound and approach eventually point at something intimate: the ‘how to be’. A shared ‘something’ we truly celebrate together via media at hand.”​ A part of proceeds will go to Isaakov dog shelter in Petropavl, Kazakhstan. The artists heard on this anthology are: s[].any, goo, lycopsid_,  OL,  sidechain unit, tumy, free version, other joe, louis vogue,  яома bantik ³³³,  obe,  s.drift,  double blind,  Alien Recycling,  obi uto,  moemu, zuno,  Infant,  Kilou,  virtual echo,  DJ Birdbath,  kk.Shucko,  marat koshkin,  Yerofeyev,  16:9 ratio,  duun,  ebilen, inferior design,  Alien Team,  slyn, poole,  bad lsd trips,  defkon, and Sta Dormida. Curated by a b, marat koshkin & a. doina, Mostly mastered by yeyo & a b. Artwork by marat koshkin & a. doina. Merch design by marat koshkin. One of the best aspects of anthologies is that smaller projects have the opportunity to exhibit in a common showcase, reaching more of the whole community, to expose their work and to experience the reactions. None of the tracks are very long, the shortest one is less than one minute. If something puts you off, hang on, there will be something new coming along soon, or maybe more of the same but somehow different. Some aspects are similar, but each track stands alone. The names are creative, to decode this, here you will find the moniker of the creating entity, a hyphen, followed by the track title and the length in minutes, and a brief description of what I think that I heard. 1. s[].any – t.here 05:55 — Opens into a dark mood, I imagine that I hear many voices hidden in the mix, which is a sound collage, with different surprises. Our dreamy poetic singer is honest, the overall sound has lots of little flavors in a delicious complex collage stew. So strange. 2. goo – Secret 03:37 — A classical guitar, with some electronics whirled about, a cello, a singer, a robot plumber. Fragments of voices that echo amidst the tunneling strings and things. Easy drifting instrumentals with strange effects and odd bits here and there. 3. lycopsid_ – raupe 03:40 — “Lycopsid” is a botanical term for clubmosses, and Lycopsid (or lycopsid) is a Leipzig, Germany-based musical artist, known for producing electronic or ambient music, with tracks available on platforms like Bandcamp and Pandora. The sound here is celestial, a steady awakening into increasing brightness with interesting sound collages or wet chattering bits sprinkled and patterned about. 4. OL – Softshell 02:08 — The collected cadence is a bit loose, mumbling taps and tings, shuffling percussive snaps and shudders. It lunges forward, it pauses and holds, it shifts and prepares to lunge, it starts again. I can dig it. It whispers to me about beats while staying fluid and just flowing with sticky stop-start moments built in. 5. sidechain unit – wasted youth riddim 03:32 — I think there are voices, fragments including screaming happy kids in a playground hidden within the mix, which comes up harsh and stays very interesting, percussive clacks, perhaps some island riddim, there are ghosts flicker dancing, and a roller coaster where they all scream together. The beat is skeletal, with an odd missing beat pattern and new mumbling taps and tings, shuffling percussive snaps and shudders. 6. tumy – frostlings 03:48 — A dusty ghost piano melody loop and an agitated electronic spirit bouncing about, echo effects gone wild, in a deep dub style. There are many things going on at once, the piano, and percussive elements that echo and shatter, about half way through the strange beat gets stronger. The piano stays perfectly on course. 7. free version – moonlight yuh spotlight yuh 06:05 — Somewhere in the abandoned old factory ruins by the sea, in a big dark cave there are strange radios playing, or maybe poetic people reciting lines, or both and more. This sounds like it is probably dangerous, voices are talking and there are echoes, plenty of water. I do not understand any words, which are mostly repetitive. There are large monsters moving about off in the distance, I hear some smoothly running machine noises and banging about. And more water. 8. other joe – every image (ft. concave reflection) 04:28 — A piano, people breathing, someone is talking, there is some kind of electronic instrument, nice and slow. Mystery at every moment, dripping water, maybe a flute, odd woodwinds, slow and quiet and cautious, full of microscopic details. Spraying water? The piano keeps dreaming and seems distant sometimes. The bowed drones have the sky here. 9. louis vogue – out of reach (ft. saga charlotte) 00:59 — Louis Vogue is an electronic music artist, DJ, and co-founder of the Brussels-based collective and event series Club Détour, known for playing atmospheric and experimental sets on Kiosk Radio. The short dreamy misty track bursts in, I hear drama, sadness and darkness on a sweeping scale, singing over the storm of glitchy-pitched musical tones. 10. яома bantik ³³³ – ₉⁹₉ (yeyo & a b edit) 02:16 — ЯOMA BANTIK @romabantik is a Russian artist from the Urals, working with metal, natural and industrial heritages. I hear a fella and his guitar, strummin’ and singin’, sounds great to me. Good times, with no serious fancy science fiction studio effects. A young man alone, telling his heart. 11. obe – iji’s dub 06:37 — I think this one feels like we are deep underwater, the throbbing reverb feels like a dub mix, with various bouncing pulse echoes, the playful living echo vibration creature crawls about above the constant pulse flowing inward slowly then flowing outward, repeating, like breathing in your sleep. The dark water flows for miles below us. There are UFOs down there too. 12. s.drift – quatro CD 03:50 — Nervous  and clicky like a rhythm, or maybe more like a collage, with odd forward and backward sounds, blending into a lighter abstract clicky beat, maybe adding a hi hat cymbal effect, an unexpected voice beep pops by a few times, while the shadows shake and shimmy. A drum set somehow shows up. We step forth with pep. 13. double blind – fade 02:29 — Water flowing, strange environmental humming rings, with mysterious winds and rain. The voice sounds drained and perhaps coming from another world. The message is in the form of hopeful poetry, and is not obvious. In my mind’s eye I see candles in the misty rings. 14. Alien Recycling – Pareidolia Cat Dub 03:44 — I am always trying to find meaningful faces or messages in musical clouds or in chaos. Here is an electronic cat that slides. There is an echo rhythm beat, drawing some space night ramblers. The beat is not steady and nearly seems to fall apart, and rallies a few times then eases off. I have been feeding that cat. 15. obi uto – oysq 03:33 — Perhaps this is just how they talk, strange beeps and clicking-rushing tones. No beats, no words, plenty of odd looping collage fragmentations, pulling from a unique musique concrete style and beyond. The feeling is restless. 16. moemu, zuno – petal traces 04:47 — Moemu and zuno are two musical artists associated with ambient, electronic, chill-out music contexts or lo-fi soundscapes, often featured in mix sets, and are found on Pandora and Bandcamp. I hear fragments of so many things, dark loop dreams that make no sense but are restful, pouring spilling cascading repeating flowing falling scattering evaporating, restless and gently convulsive, chaotic, there are void ghosts and melancholia floods over the roller coasters. I try to get there early and stay late. 17. Infant – jewel 03:01 — From twitchy robot bleeps to greebles rumbling, coming through a small tube with some shortwave radio throbbing and ringing, or maybe they are simply talking amongst themselves. There are  little spinning bumping bells and a tap-ring collage. A beat comes about, explodes and gets wild, smooths and bumps along, the flow always gets busy in places after the extended coasting interludes. soak vol 2 by Kilou   18. Kilou – Blurry 03:40 — Somewhere deep in space we float upside down, feet over eyebrows, there is buzzing and a musical instrument strumming lightly. Some guy is singing while the dragons and other monsters size the room. Soon chains are broken. A guy is talking and singing, playing a guitar, flying feathered electronic snakes swirling about, seeking a hole in outer space. I hear strumming, spare shovels and  tapping glasses with ice. I didn’t tell you everything. 19. virtual echo – j trip 04:35 — In the wash water, jiggling as the machine works, the sloshing water sets the beat. I hear nifty chattering little rhythms and throbbing waves of activities, her voices echo, skyrockets splash, there may be a drum kit, and now we are cooking, throbbing right along. This is where I belong. 20. DJ Birdbath – Rose Drip 04:06 — DJ Birdbath is the artist name for Ian Baxter, an electronic music producer based in the South Island of New Zealand, known for ambient and experimental music, often featuring deconstructed sounds, fragmented rhythms, and shoegaze-tinged vocals influenced by his past, often using a mix of real and generated samples. His music is featured on NTS Radio, SoundCloud, and Bandcamp. He released the album Memory Empathy (2024) via Theory Therapy, which features a blend of samples and influences from his time in the UK. The sound here is an abstract beat pattern that never stops changing, loops with flowing chaos and surprises, mostly variations on the instrumental constructions. Somewhere about half way in, they settle into a very catchy complex groove that stays uncertain but keeps going. They fly off, they fade. 21. kk.Shucko – another missed mirage 03:26 — kk.Shucko is an San Francisco-based experimental club producer and DJ known for crafting intricate, high-res techno, IDM, and warped drum and bass soundscapes, her sets revel in composing evenings that sew together soft and hard, continuity and catharsis draw listeners into an alien realm, and fuses needy rhythms, ambient, and club music to create immersive, imagined biomes. Associated with Club Moniker and Ommaya Records, they create “hyperspace” audio, often incorporating elements like glass and gel, and hold a residency at SutroFM. I hear energized chattering electronic squirrels, also scratchy electronified voices painted on the air. The squirrels keep me busy, some of the sound is harsh with whispers hidden inside, hit with sharp short and zappy bolts, melting into a bubbling sea of writhing monsters and phantoms. Darned cool. 22. marat koshkin – cry OS 03:37 — Marat Koshkin is a musician and artist from Petropavlovsk, Kazakhstan, recently located in Saint-Petersburg. The beat is catchy from the jump, splashy weaving beats stay strong and powerful mixed with the collage nicely, gettin’ jammy with multiple instruments, gettin’ down within the change and solids. A winsome laugh has been captured. 23. Yerofeyev – Smares (Senglar Rmx) 05:52 — Senglar is an electronic music artist and composer known for producing experimental, atmospheric, immersive, often dark, and downtempo electronic soundscapes. Based on recent music releases, Senglar often works within the niche of electronic, ambient, and downtempo genres, featuring 2024 album releases like Sensen – Hum. A rolling ball of fragmented multisounds, shortwave abstract whispers, electronic complex and plenty to listen to per sparkle, great for head rushes and surprises. I am sure there is more to the story as to how Senglar came to remix Yerofeyev’s Smares. 24. 16:9 ratio – Nothing Drive 03:15 — 16:9 ratio is likely the moniker for Geunf, a multidisciplinary artist, DJ, and producer based in Ottawa, Canada. He is known for blending techno, pop, and deconstructed club music. He released the ambient/experimental project Our Keyboards in 2025. He is also a member of the pop trio Los3r. I hear a children’s playground and people talking just out of reach, the beat trots up and off we go with nice propulsion, dancing snowflakes, the feeling defines royal and grand (both), towards the end we are at a full gallop with happily laughing snare drums and a big wow finish. 25. duun – chill! 03:28 — A machine is dancing inside of a twisting huge towering steel monster, I sense a dark voodoo beach with a moonlight fire, the rolling beat goes on and on, the feeling is fearsome and close, I hear a sly dark dub beat, probably from a strong dancing doom machine. 26. ebilen – aeon 04:00 — Ebilen is an electronic music artist known for tracks like “Strange Emotion” and the album pihkal (Base 1), releasing music through labels like Tabula Rasa Records and featuring on SoundCloud. They produce in genres often associated with underground electronic or ambient styles. I am in outer space, no gravity, no up or down, spinning slowly, whispers always getting more complex, shifting and ticking inside the mind. Something changes, the energizing chaos dance continues while ghosts call in the dark empty corridors, tiny punchy robot construction workers appear everywhere all at once for a little while, things continue to change, finally we finish swirling with whispers and the clock ticks. 27. inferior design – conning 04:47 — Outer space has no corners or answers, aliens and robots scoot along as we explore all these little pieces, like sand only smaller and with more shapes and colors, flashing and glittering particles spreading everywhere. There is no gravity so the spinning can seem slower, granular overstimulation transports some to a new place with new possibilities. Now we are having a sunrise inside the chaos collage, shooting lasers across the tracks, as chaos echoes and bumps about. This too shall morph. 28. Alien Team – my team 03:33 — Somewhere way out there, by a waterfall, the birdbeams call as they rush by. The rumbling loop brings up the low end, the birdbeams come and go, now we have a beat rumble stomp shake throbstep march while the birdbeams swirl overhead. A continuation of rushing water, with new strange birds taking over and proliferating, growing and developing, learning to dance. Soon the tribe is grooving. Now we are at the waterfall with the chaos birds. I woke up wondering where I was. At home of course. 29. slyn, poole – arc 04:18 — Slyn, a Glasgow-based sound artist, live performer, and DJ, is known for immersive, experimental, and eccentric club sounds that blend IDM, bass, and jungle with ambient textures, heavily influenced by a background in marine biology and themes of hydrofeminism and queer ecology, with soundscapes that are often described as underwater, dreamy, or “algae-like.” I am seeking more about Poole. What I hear here is a new jungle of fabrics and textures, mysterious vocalisms, many things at once. There is a primitive beat picking up, I hear the jungle in the distance. Now and then some guitar tapping time baps along. I want to live here under the arc. 30. bad lsd trips – eno river 04:46 — bad lsd trips is a collaborative music project between artists Domingo Castillo Flores and Mónica Mesa (who performs as doris dana). Based in Miami, Florida, the duo formed during the pandemic, producing music that blends elements of early industrial, dark ambient, tape music, and drone “psychedelic meditations” and “murky field recordings” with “ASMR-adjacent synths.” My mind melts, I hear strange twisted whistles, an emerging beat like a train rattle power turnip ringing shards of metal along comes the boat, an odd motor throb whispering starshine flotters about and the motor keeps running. The individual words are lost for me, the poetic tone and vibe are clear and strong, I float off into another dream with newer words that are never easier to remember. 31. defkon – sun tunnels 03:04 — We are building a new solar passageway, and adding a piano loop skeleton with strange attachments and things to tap. The piano stays solid while the changes bring new creatures that make sound, odd new sounds, piano loops and wild improv with little hand instruments adding into the pattern. 32. Sta Dormida – Trace Abruption 04:44 — Sta Dormida is an independent musical artist, singer-songwriter, producer, and audio engineer who composes, records, produces, mixes, and masters their own music. Known for releases such as Ace of Grace (2025), More Like Never (2025), and It’s Rigged (2024), they are active on platforms like Spotify and Bandcamp. This contribution features her singing and playing classical guitar, nothing electronic, just dry fingers on strings and layered singing. I want to stay here forever. A former circus aerialist, she pioneered the male-dominated industry in the early 1900s by mastering traditional hand-poked (“stick-and-poke”) tattooing, helping to introduce tattoo artistry to inland America. soak vol 2 is available on soak. items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自哈萨克斯坦独立厂牌Soak的合辑，收录32首碎片化、情感化的当代实验电子作品。专辑以angular和granular电子声为基础，融合downtempo、lamebient、声音设计及原始/加工的亲密声响，展现了国际艺术家社区的前卫创作力。短曲目结构（约1分钟）强调快速变换与即兴感，每首作品虽短却独立完整，整体指向一种关于「如何存在」的亲密探索。作为非主流地区的独立发行，该合辑呈现了东欧、中亚与全球实验音乐场景的独特视角与文化多样性，对关注实验电子与前卫声音的听众具有较高的参考价值。

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 970Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. Their debut album 'On The Sunday Of Life'' was released in 1991. It's a selection of compositions from earlier unofficial cassette releases. The first 'full-fledged' album of Porcupine Tree isn't only an exhibition of the young artist's most interesting ideas, not only the essence of creative work concentrated in the psychedelic convention which Wilson undertook in the second half of the 80's, but is a compelling work, by all means enigmatic, mysterious, shrouded in an aura of unreality. It collects Wilson's favourite songs from those years into a double album. Listening in retrospect, we may well find pretty nonplussed at this highly experimental mixture of psychedelic and space rock, moving from ambient flute pieces to the sort of whimsical nonsense that wouldn't be out of place on the early Pink Floyd's releases.The line up 'On The Sunday Of Life'' is composed by Steven Wilson (vocals, guitar and other instruments like keyboards and programming). 'On The Sunday Of Life'' also has the participation of some other musicians. So, we also have here the presence of Malcolm Stocks 'Solomon St. Jemain' (vocals and additional guitars), Master Timothy Masters (oboe) and John Marshall (drums), as the guest musicians of the album.'On The Sunday Of Life'' has eighteen tracks. 'Music For The Head' is very short, a kind of an introduction to the album. It has a rather sinister tone, with some nice flute work to go with it. 'Jupiter Island' is from Wilson's adolescent days. It's a charming psychedelic tune with lyrics that features some fast paced drumming, apparently from a drum machine. The next pieces are two highly experimental short pieces. 'Third Eye Surfer' is a nice dissonant song with an odd metered drum improvisation along with synths and keys. The title track is an atmospheric piece dominated by the keyboards with a lot of sounds. Both pieces form two relaxed pieces on the album. 'The Nostalgia Factory' is the second song on the album including lyrics. This is a very nice psychedelic song with a great beat where the vocals sound distinctly due to the vocoder. The next two are yet more experimental pieces with some rather sinister spoken dialog. 'Space Transmission' is mostly spoken again through a vocoder. It's a very dark and ambient track. 'Message From A Self-Destructing Turnip' is another spoken piece, a very short ambient break piece. Both are psychedelic at its extreme. 'Radioactive Toy' is an interesting psychedelic epic with nice heavy guitar melodies and slowly pounding drums. It still is one of the favourite Porcupine Tree's songs played live as an encore. It has stood up to the test of time amazingly well. 'Nine Cats' is a nice acoustic track despite being very simple. It continues to emphasize the eclectic nature of the album. It became a fan's favourite that was rarely performed live. 'Hymn' is another short instrumental that has some strange vocal sounds and synths. It's more of a soundscape interlude between songs. 'Footprints' is also from Wilson's adolescent days. It also reminds me of Pink Floyd in Syd Barrett's era. It's another song with lyrics, guitar and synths. The next two tracks continue to absorb Pink Floyd's early influences. 'Linton Samuel Dawson' is awesomely weird and frenetic but very fun too. It's based on psychedelic drums and some mind blowing strange vocals through a vocoder. 'And The Swallows Dance Above The Sun' is another semi obscure odd track with a drum machine beat combined with ambient keyboards and vocals. 'Queen Quotes Crowley' is technically an instrumental. It has many psychedelic effects with some nice guitar work and where the vocals are in the reverse. The two next tracks are the final short instrumentals of this album. 'No Luck With Rabbits' is a very short experimental instrumental of synths, a kind of a soundscape between songs. 'Begonia Seduction Scene' is a lovely instrumental with some great acoustic guitar work and synths. 'This Long Silence' is a psychedelic up-tempo song that again features vocals through a vocoder. It follows the same style as some other songs, a good indication of what is to follow. 'It Will Rain For A Million Years' is another track that points the direction that the band would later take. There are hardly any lyrics on this song. Most of it is instrumental and ambient. It features a nice guitar work supported by a heavy rhythm, a good way to close the album.Conclusion: 'On The Sunday Of Life...' although in its moments heralds the later stylistic development of the band, as a whole is rather a sign of its time, a testimony to the band's interesting genesis. However, this doesn't diminish its value. It's a unique album, an extremely eclectic work. It treats this eclecticism as a method of surrealistic expression. It has its standout tracks, mainly 'Radioactive Toy', 'Nine Cats' and 'It Will Rain For A Million Years' that are worth the price of the purchase alone, but also features plenty of filler that you'll either enjoy for what it is or skip past every time. Nonetheless, for Porcupine Tree's fans, this album is of course a must to get to know the beginnings of the band and the roots of their later works. Still, I think it can be rather misleading for those who want to get to know the band. Anyhow and despite 'On The Sunday Of Life...' isn't as mature as later Porcupine Tree's stuff it still is recommendable.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)
items._cn_summary: Porcupine Tree的首张专辑展现出浓郁的前卫实验气质，将迷幻摇滚与空间摇滚深度融合，并大量运用合成器、鼓机编程和环境音效，营造出神秘且具超现实色彩的听觉氛围。专辑收录了从早期卡带作品中精选的18首曲目，从氛围 flute 引入到重型吉他旋律，风格跨度大且充满即兴感。虽然是1992年的发行，但其电子音效设计与当代实验音乐语境仍有共鸣，尤其符合偏好实验/前卫与电子音乐的用户群体。作品兼具探索性与可听性，是了解英式前卫摇滚演变的重要文献。

items.excerpt: Weil in ihrer Heimat USA die Auftrittsmöglichkeiten und die Akzeptanz des Publikums fehlen, ziehen die Musiker des Art Ensemble Of Chicago im Juni 1969 nach Paris. items.body: Weil in ihrer Heimat USA die Auftrittsmöglichkeiten und die Akzeptanz des Publikums fehlen, ziehen die Musiker des Art Ensemble Of Chicago im Juni 1969 nach Paris. Dort trifft ihre multistilistische experimentelle Musik auf ein dankbares Publikum und auf Plattenlabels, denen nicht erst erklärt werden muss, dass Jazz auch anders als Louis Armstrong klingen kann. Während des knapp zweijährigen Frankreich-Aufenthalts entstehen mehr als ein Dutzend Alben, People In Sorrow ist eines der ersten davon. Mit dem Titelstück, das sich über zwei LP-Seiten erstreckt, gelingt Trompeter Lester Bowie, Bassist Malachi Favors, Joseph Jarman und Roscoe Mitchell an diversen Blas- und Percussioninstrumenten ein Musterbeispiel der freien Kollektivimprovisation. Free Jazz, afrikanische Musik, europäische Kunstmusik und Klassik verschmelzen in einer musikalischen Erzählung, die über 40 Minuten zu keinem Zeitpunkt langweilig wird. Vor allem die »little instruments«, die Percussioninstrumente und die Nicht-Instrumente, prägen den Sound: Irgendwo klingelt immer ein Glöckchen, ertönt ein Gong oder scheppert ein Becken. Das kontrastiert die freien Ausbrüche der Blasinstrumente und erzeugt immer wieder einen Spannungsbogen. Nicht zuletzt bringt das Art Ensemble den Faktor Humor in eine Musikrichtung, die gewöhnlich als komplett unlustig gilt.
items._cn_summary: Art Ensemble Of Chicago在1969年巴黎时期录制的重要作品，展现了自由爵士、非洲音乐与欧洲古典元素的多层融合。四十余分钟的超长标题曲以小打击乐器、非传统乐器与人声噪音为核心，与管乐的自由即兴形成动态张力，整体结构紧凑而不显冗长。作为自由爵士与实验爵士的先驱团体，Art Ensemble在这张专辑中奠定了独特的声响美学，将即兴演奏推向集体叙事的高度，同时注入幽默感。专辑体现了强烈的前卫精神与跨文化视野，对于偏好实验与自由爵士的听眾具有重要的参考价值。

items.body: Das Duo Phantom Horse liefert auf Primal Forms Tracks, die zwischen Ambient, Industrial und experimenteller Elektronik oszillieren und dabei dennoch in sich stimmig bleiben. Auf dem Debütalbum Different Forces (2015) klangen Phantom Horse noch leichter, konventioneller, weniger düster. Elf Jahre später bedienen sich die beiden deutschen Musiker sich einer kraftvollen Soundpalette, die Synthie mit spacigen Tönen, Static Noise und Percussion kombiniert. Das Cover von Primal Forms ist mit Farbtönen bedruckt, die nahtlos ineinander übergehen. Dieses Muster setzt sich auch in der Musik des Duos um Ulf Schütte und Niklas Dommaschk fort. Die Tracks bestehen aus zahlreichen Spuren, die so übereinandergelegt werden, dass sie in einer vielschichtigen Soundkulisse münden. Jeder Track wirkt wie ein Bild, dem man beim Entstehen zusieht. »Primal Forms«, der zweite Track des gleichnamigen Albums, beginnt mit einer einzelnen Tonspur, über die sich ein funkenartiges, hohes Geräusch legt. Dann kommen immer mehr Spuren dazu. Wie viele Stücke dieser Platte fängt auch dieses ohne Melodie an; erst nach einiger Zeit legt sie sich über technischen Percussion-Sound. So entsteht komplexe Musik, in der man immer wieder etwas Neues heraushört. Vielfältige Tempi erzeugen vielschichtige Soundbilder, die langen Songs wirken aufgrund ihrer Vielseitigkeit kürzer, als sie es eigentlich sind.
items._cn_summary: Phantom Horse是来自德国的二人电子组合，其新专辑Primal Forms融合了环境音乐、工业声响和实验性电子音乐。相较于2015年的前作，这张专辑呈现出更为黑暗和复杂的声响景观，通过多层音轨叠加构建起丰富的声音织体。专辑中的曲目往往从单一音轨起始，逐步叠加高频静电噪音和合成器音色，最终在技术性打击乐节奏中形成多维度的声场。复杂的编曲结构使音乐在变幻莫测的同时保持内聚力，节奏变化丰富，长曲目反而显得紧凑。德国独立电子场景的这张作品在实验性和技术性上都达到了较高水准，与偏好实验、前卫、电子和暗潮音乐的用户群体高度契合。

items.body: This single slipped our radar but is more than worth announcing. A few weeks ago the Belgian electronic project Kilmarth released “Avant de céder…“, a three-track instrumental digital single combining glitch, dark minimal, and experimental electronic textures. Written, produced, and mixed by Cedric Wattergniaux, the release is available on Bandcamp. The three tracks are a first glimpse of ayet unnamed forthcoming album. Note that the third track is a reimagined version of an earlier Kilmarth piece. Avant de céder… by Kilmarth Four months ago, in January 2026, Wattergniaux released the concept album “Cherophobia” through Adventurous Music, the Leipzig-based micro-label focused on experimental electronic works. That nine-track album explored the fear of happiness, and featured seven guest vocalists including Deranged Psyche, Mad Mac, Eeerisei, Silly Shadow, Heri B., Natasha Moreno, and Clémence Legrand. About Kilmarth Kilmarth is a Belgian electronic solo project founded in 2007 by composer, producer, and French teacher Cédric Wattergniaux. The project name references Kilmarth, the Cornish house at the centre of Daphne du Maurier’s novel The House on the Strand. The project debuted in 2018 with the CD mini-album “Catharsis”. In 2021, Wattergniaux issued the EP “Derrière Le Miroir”, which pushed into minimal-electro and cinematic territory and later produced the video-focused single “M-Fia41”. A Side-Line interview from 2018, “Music Is A Legal Drug That Has The Immense Power To Make Us Escape”, offers further background on the project’s origins. In 2022, he released the two-track single “Baryum”, introducing a darker post-industrial ambient angle. The 2023 mini-album “Better Days” introduced a singer for the first time in the project’s history. January 2024 saw the release of “Sociological Veranda”, Wattergniaux’s first full-length IDM album, combining dark electro, glitch, ambient, drum and bass, and cinematic elements across its tracklist. That same year, the single “Vergessen” appeared with the jazz-infused B-side “ToExposeTheTruth”. In November 2024, the EP “My Son of The Moon” followed. In early 2025, Kilmarth collaborated with D-Fried on the album “Micrometeoritic Flowerpot”. The “Cherophobia” concept album for Adventurous Music arrived in January 2026. “Avant de céder…” followed two months later and is available on Kilmarth’s Bandcamp page.
items._cn_summary: 比利时电子单人项目Kilmarch的最新三轨单曲，融合glitch、dark minimal与实验电子声响。这是其即将发布的未命名专辑的首个预告，延续了艺术家Cédric Wattergniaux在IDM、暗潮与工业电子领域的探索脉络。作品强调氛围构建与声音实验，呈现典型的独立实验电子美学。作为一个自2007年成立以来持续深耕地下电子场景的项目，Kilmarth保持着相对低调但风格一致的艺术表达。该单曲通过Bandcamp独立发行，展现了欧洲独立电子音乐的扎实功底与对实验边界的持续探索。

items.body: Along with the reissue of “Ritual”, which appeared on CD for the first time, Zoharum is simultaneously releasing this album by Wieloryb. “God’s Final Breath” was released only in digital format via Antyscena last year and is now finally receiving a CD edition as well, although without the bonus tracks. If you are familiar with Paweł Kmiecik’s Polish project, you will immediately recognize his affinity for Rhythmic-Noise, while also appreciating the way he uses it as a foundation to incorporate Trance/Tribal influences alongside additional Electro elements. The result is an exhilarating production in which power and dark atmospheres merge with hard-hitting beats, provoking frenetic dancefloor energy in the listener. Here and there, raw, possessed vocals are added -and according to me these tracks are the best ones- while other tracks reveal subtle yet highly effective EBM influences. One particular piece even recalls the era when Ministry fully embraced an Industrial direction, although Wieloryb reshapes this into a kind of Industrial-Ambient/Cinematic experience. This is an extremely versatile opus; perhaps not the definitive reference album in Wieloryb’s catalogue, yet still a highly successful release containing several essential and crushing musical gems. For me, Wieloryb remains one of the most visionary projects within the broader Industrial scene. (Rating:8). Listen to “Break The Chains”: https://zoharum.bandcamp.com/track/break-the-chains
items._cn_summary: 波兰音乐人Paweł Kmiecik以Wieloryb项目推出的这张专辑，深度融合了节奏噪音、部落舞曲与电子元素，呈现出暗黑氛围感强、节拍硬朗的工业电子声响。专辑巧妙地将狂热的舞池能量与受Ministry启发的工业质地相结合，融入环境与电影感的声场，同时保留了原始的EBM影响与人声表现力。作为波兰独立厂牌Zoharum发行的小众作品，这张专辑展现了高度的音乐融合性与独特的工业电子美学，与用户偏好的暗潮、电子与实验风格形成良好对应。乐评人给出了8分的高评价，认为虽然可能不是该艺人最标志性的作品，但仍包含数首值得关注的重量级曲目。

On the Corner (Columbia Records, 1972) Abrasive, Alcoholic, Anarchic, Anticlimax, Aphrodisiac, Arrogant, Autoimmune, Barbaric, Belligerent, Brash, Challenging, Contagious, Controversial, Cruel, Cubist, Cynical, Dangerous, Disloyal, Disturbing, Divining, Dizzy, Electrifying, Engaging, Essential, Evocative, Exhilarating, Expressionist, Fearless, Fussy, Futurist, Ghastly, Greasy, Grumpy, Hallucinogenic, Hardcore, Heavenly, Hypnotic, Infernal, Inflammable, Innocent, Intriguing, Irritating, Labyrinthine, Liberating, Loud, Magnetic, Material, Meaningless, Metropolitan, Monochrome, Mysterious, Neon, Neurasthenic, Nocturnal, Oblique, Obnoxious, Ominous, Polluted, Polychromatic, Pornographic, Precursory, Pretentious, Primal, Psychotropic, Quirky, Quixotic, Raw, Reckless, Rusty, Saturated, Self-indulgent, Sexy, Spiraling, Syncretic, Telluric, Temperamental, Timeless, Toxic, Uncanny, Uncompromising, Unruly, Vibrant, Visionary, Vulgar, Wicked, Xenomorphic, Yucky, Zippy: QUINTESSENTIAL, BLACK, MILES. - Ferruccio Martinotti ESP (Columbia Records, 1965) Miles Davis’s second great quintet put a fantastic four behind the great leader: Wayne Shorter, Herbie Hancock, Ron Carter, and Tony Williams. Their 1965 ESP is the perfect result. Miles was the philosopher’s stone: put him in the presence of a potential genius stuck in a rut, two virtuosos coming to the studio with mediocre melodies, or two simple chords longing for each other and the right hands on the keyboard…and you got pure gold. It helps if you have a crush on Shorter and Hancock. If you have been touched by the former’s Juju , or the latter’s Empyrean Isles you will feel your heart fluttering awake. The mood is pensive, sadly romantic (but in a good way), and always extending the witch’s finger. It doesn’t get better than this, just different and rarely as delicious. - Kenneth Blanchard --- Miles Davis and the Modern Jazz Giants (Prestige, 1956) Miles Davis and the Modern Jazz Giants was the first Miles Davis record I ever heard. It was a well-played LP in my Dad’s collection that I stumbled upon in my first year of college and for some reason, I decided to spin it. This was almost my first encounter with jazz at all — except some big band stuff in Abbott and Costello movies — and I would find it hard to convey the immediate wonderment I felt listening to Milt Jackson’s opening to “ The Man I Love ” (take 2). Milt Jackson’s vibes weren’t the point to that track, and they're not the point to this encomium, but, like the Yellow Brick Road, that opening led me to an extraordinary, life-changing experience. I still wonder why nobody plays vibes like that, and I still wonder what it is about Miles’ non-muted take on the melody that hearing it — and Monk, Red Garland, and Coltrane — was like nothing before or since, for me. Tutu (Warner Bros., 1986) The first new Miles Davis record that came out after hearing that was Tutu . Forty years separate me from that first listen, and thirty years separate Tutu from “ The Man I Love. ” I still enjoy Tutu quite a lot. All the tunes were written by or with producer/bassist, Marcus Miller — much as all the tunes from Miles’ 2nd quintet were written by Wayne Shorter — but there was no mistaking that Miles led the sessions and that it was Miles Davis music. I would be lying if I said Tutu was as high in my estimation as the Prestige record, but the things that make Miles' music the ineffable thing it is are present in both cases. There’s a sweetness and melancholy in the ever-present harmon mute. His melodies are treated just so, and his improvisations seem inevitable. Also, possibly because of the space he leaves or the example he sets, he improves every musician he works with (except maybe Monk, but there’s a story behind that). So much time has passed, but this music still fires off my endorphins. Wonderful. - Gary Chapin --- Ascenseur pour l'échafaud Soundtrack (Fontana, 1958) Paris is the perfect city to film at night, in black and white, with its streetlights and shadows in soft focus. It’s the perfect city to film beautiful Jeanne Moreau as she walks without direction searching for her missing lover, passing brightly lit cafés and dimly lit alleys, stumbling in a daze through traffic. And Miles Davis’s plaintive trumpet makes the perfect music to accompany her, the perfect music to furtively whisper “Je t’aime”, the perfect music to commit a murder for love…and the perfect music to get stuck in an elevator while trying to make your escape. Miles Davis recorded the soundtrack for Louis Malle’s debut film Ascenseur pour l'échafaud (Elevator To The Gallows) by improvising while watching the film. It’s a great film in its own right, a terrific blend of noir tropes, and it’s one of the first films of the French New Wave. But it’s the soundtrack that makes it an all-time classic. - Richard Blute Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评围绕Miles Davis横跨三十年的四张专辑展开，涵盖1972年实验融合力作《On the Corner》、1965年调式爵士经典《ESP》、1956年硬波普录音《Miles Davis and the Modern Jazz Giants》以及1986年融合流行电子的《Tutu》。评论采用形容词罗列与第一人称叙事相结合的方式，尤其对《On the Corner》的实验性与《ESP》中五重奏的哲学性描述深入。Miles Davis作为爵士乐革新者，其作品在调式爵士、融合爵士、电子爵士等领域均有突破性探索，与用户对实验、前卫及学院派爵士的偏好高度契合。乐评强调了音乐的前卫精神与历史意义，揭示了Davis如何将爵士与funk、摇滚、电子等跨界元素融合的独特路径。

items.album: Twilight Of Perception Redux Volume Three 1996- 2006
items.excerpt: Here’s the third volume in the Twilight Of Perception series.  Each three-CD set in this series serves up a selection of rare and unreleased tracks from between the mid 1990’s and early 2000’s by Euro ambient pioneer Vidna Obmana, aka Dirk Serries. The set features eighteen tracks in all, with a good variation in both the tone and atmosphere, moving from lulling n’drifting ambience, all the way through upbeat / rhythmic-edged ethnic ambient works.
items._cn_summary: 这是欧洲氛围先驱Vidna Obmana（Dir Serries）1996至2006年间稀有未发行作品集第三卷，收录十八首曲目。音乐跨度从催眠式的漂移氛围到充满节奏感的民族氛围实验，展现了跨十余年创作阶段的风格演变。作为独立地下发行的小众选集，项目本身具有文献价值与探索性，其实验氛围与民族元素的融合符合用户对实验、前卫及世界音乐的偏好，同时契合电子音乐与暗潮风格的审美取向。

items.body: Review by arymenezes — My impressions of this work were taken from the youtube videos of Dikajee's channel on youtube.A beautiful guitar, along with vocalizations and a singing style very similar to Mariana Semkina, opens the album. Dikajee doesn't have the same clarity and lucidity as Mariana does; however, I remind you that this is Dikajee's first album. So, let's return to my observations about it. The harmonies develop a magnificent sense of balance between the strings, the rhythmic section, and the meter of the phrases, half sung and half recited. Dikajee saves the high notes (there are a few, therefore they are used moderately) more for the end of the song, where the instrumental also grows. The images of the artist in the middle of a forest, with trees, a frozen lake, and what appear to be spirits or supernatural entities, are well produced, although they didn't make much sense to me. Splendid opening and closing. Instrumental score 10, vocals 8.5.Dikajee's vocals, his presence, and movements in the promotional video are very captivating on the beginning of the next track. The different layers of his singing, the inventive rhythms, are the artistic and vital epicenter of this composition. The piano gently and lovingly surrounds all of this until the percussion enters, which adds firmness and robustness to the whole ensemble. A short pause in the middle takes the song to a more intimate vibe, and also provides an interlude for a different approach, a kind of a mystical march, that harmoniously and spontaneously transforms itself to reach a more complete rhythmic section. Meanwhile, in the video, the sculptures by Archil Didishvilli, which had already appeared before, now provide a backdrop for the visual and conceptual aesthetic presented. At this moment, I realize how Dikajee's singing tends to be whispered, and therefore I can't identify most of what she's singing (even though, english is not my native language). Instrumental 9, vocals 9.A very captivating and clear guitar cradles me in the opening of the 3rd track. The cello provides a beautiful counterpoint with its low notes, and fits very well on the current transformation from gentleness into a kind of walking rhythm of the song. The acoustic guitar gives way to the harmonies of more strings, before a viola or fiddle develops a gentle and maternal solo. It's impressive how the notes never fight or disagree with each other, making it look easy to be a great musician. The sonic mass gradually increases with astonishing fluidity at one point, but the composition returns to a more intimate approach at its very end. While writing this review, I am naturally drawn to want to listen to each song again, given the impact this work has had on me. And a fundamental factor in this enchantment is that in contemporary progressive rock there are many very noisy works, whether due to guttural vocals, the weight of the sound produced, and/or the exaggerated number of notes "per second". This album by Dikajee allows you to follow everything with clarity, discernment, and no hurry or excess. Score 9.The artist's next song was the one that (casually) allowed me to acknowledge Dikajee. Here, the singing is much less whispered and more mezzo-soprano. Once again (other two tracks has the same proposal), the piano is the only element accompanying her on the entrance. But gradually, as quite enigmatic and deep vocalizations emerges, meanwhile more musical elements are broughten. The video, using gray/black tones, desolating images, and ruined environments, combines very well with the musical atmosphere. Somewhere in the middle of the song, notes fall on my ears like raindrops after the introduction, in elaborated harmonies. The phrasing is surprising and full of nuances, not only here but in several of the other tracks. Somehow, they manage to convey warmth and ice in the combination of music and visuals of this video. However, a bit more towards of the composition, the rhythmic section becomes confused and out of place, as it clashes too much with the wind instruments, bass, and strings. Fortunately, this mismatch soon disappears, and - specially - the strings become marvelous, sublime, almost apotheotic! The percussion is just absolutely precise; in fact, in general, on this snippet of the song, everything breathes and allows itself to pulse almost always perfectly. Score 8.The piano opens the fifth song quickly and without fear of being expansive. Even so, it manages to give space to the vocals, which brilliantly take advantage of this gentleness. When the percussion enters, it's time signature causes me slight discomfort, as it presents some markings that hinder the enjoyment of the melodies. This is the second time on the album that this mismatch occurs, caused solely by the percussive mass, and this time it endures a little longer, consuming and obscuring the other layers almost until the end of the song. Score 6.Starting with vocals and various instruments from the very first second wasn't a very good choice for the following track. However, at 35 seconds, they deliver a more sober and coherent atmosphere. This continues until 1min35, when they develop some rather weak percussive ideas, and very altered and robotic vocals. Furthermore, the video adds nothing, neither aesthetically, nor conceptually, nor artistically, to the song. Score 5.7.Fortunately, the 7th song, with its pleasant swing and good timing of the sections/passages, brings me back to a positive appreciation of the album. The adoption of a more electronic timbre, even though it's not so captivating, was a good choice to bring some stylistic diversity to the work. Score 7.Some good ideas are performed in the next song, with a swinging guitar. Dikajee is now elongating some of the last syllables, creating a nice musical effect. When the chorus arrives, the music becomes magnificent! Everything sounds divine. And then a penetrating and striking fiddle or viola enters. The subtleties of the rhythmic sections are incredible, and if that weren't enough, an instrument I can't identify enters, giving me goosebumps. They explore other possibilities of the chorus with magnificence and genius. Score 9.8, because they don't end the song with the same perfection.Wow, the opening of the 9th song is gorgeous. The vocals have incredibly intelligent and innovative meters. Now the lyrics are included in the video, and they are touchingly sensitive and profound. The instrumental is very economical until it reaches the 2-minute mark, but it's well-crafted, and a bit sophisticated. After this introduction, the percussion comes in for a while, but soon gives way completely to the beautiful contributions of piano, cello, and other strings. It's evident that they decided to give even more prominence to the vocals in this composition. The contribution of guest Fiona on the bagpipes falls short of my expectations. And the composition becomes a little repetitive in the final moments. Score 7.The time has come to talk about the last track. A buzzing sound interferes with the rest of the music in the first few seconds. Gladly, this buzzing disappears totally, and the sounds that could only be perceived partially now reach me with clarity and limpidity. When the vocals are added, along with a greater presence of the piano, cymbals, bass, and splendid/moderate synthesizer timbres, everything improves considerably. Dikajee's voice strikes the perfect balance between musicality and expression. Wonderful artist! The music gains momentum and grandeur, only calming down towards the very end, leaving me wanting more. Score 8.Perhaps this album, and even the entire body of her work, could be accused of being derivative of Iamthemorning and/or Renaissance. Yes, I identify numerous similarities, but Dikajee doesn't copy anything, and maybe if she does indeed seek the same style, her work is extremely original and well-crafted.Tracks 1, 2, 3, and 8 have scores between 9 and 10. The other songs range between 5.7 and 8. Final score: 4.2.

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the many Basque bands from northeastern Spain that joined the mad rush into the world ofprogressive music once unbridled artistic freedom became a reality after the collapse of the Francoregime in 1975, LISKER set itself apart from the delicate pastoral folk sounds of its Basquecontemporaries and was one of the few to fully utilize a heavier guitar fuzz infused style ofpsychedelic rock albeit with the same local folk flavors that dominated the dominating style of theera. This band from Eibor was the result of two local bands with two completely differentbackgrounds coming together. On the folk side of the equation came Ernesto G�mez (acoustic guitar, vocals) and Javier Zabala(bass) of a band called Jeki which already had a taste of success playing to an audience of over10,000 at an Anarchist Gathering in Barcelona while on the other side coming from an undergroundgarage band called Zima, a more psychedelic prototype of progressive rock that featured flautistJes�s Gil. The other two members Juli�n Alberdi (electric guitar) and Jos� Antonio Salado (drums)completed the lineup in 1978 and as LISKER released the band's sole eponymously titled album thefollowing year.While the majority of Basque prog acts with only the exception of a scant few such as Sakre wereprimarily steeped in the timeless folk traditions of the Basque heritage, LISKER was much moreinspired by the likes of Cream, Hendrix, King Crimson, Led Zeppelin, The Who and Soft Machine. Mostprominently the band featured a flute dominance that evolved the great Jethro Tull however the bandremained committed to the Basque folk flavors as its source of melodic flavoring. The band wasactive on the live circuit performing with other top Basque acts like Itoiz and Errobi as well asthe more mainstream Asfalto and others. The debut album featured five tracks that added up to 35 minutes ranging from the opening "KaleanFesta" at just over five minutes to the more progressive closer "Eldarniotik iheska" at over nine.The album mixes acoustic folk passages with a fuzz guitar dominated psychedelic rock stylereminiscent of the 1960s. The band was notable for featuring no keyboardist thus eschewing anysymphonic elements that were quite dominant on the Spanish prog scene giving LISKER a style all itsown especially within the Basque prog paradigm. The band also featured a strange rhythmic wobblethat was atypical of any other prog act of the era.The album is predominantly instrumental but does feature vocals in the Basque language. The opening"Kalean Festa" begins as a rather straightforward prog folk rock song that displays the band'ssignature conversation between the guitar and flute however as the album progresses it ratchets upthe progressive touches until the cream of the crop closer "Eldarniotik Iheska" delivers asatisfying crescendo of creative mojo firing on all pistons. The album finds that perfect balancebetween heavy psych, sensual homegrown folk rock and a spacey form of progressive rock. Overall this is a very exotic and eclectic sounding style for a Spanish prog album that may notimpress deeply upon a single exposure but is actually quite a well defined release that successfullystood out from the competition with a bold experimental touch that delivered the rock bravado to astrain of Spanish prog that was fairly resistant to the heavier and harsher sounds that predominatedthe rock scene of the era. Don't let the horrific cover art put you off as it belies the beauty ofthe contents within. Although the band existed until 1983 and was active on the live circuit, LISKERnever released a followup which is too bad because this band was one of the more innovative withinthe greater regional Basque prog scene.
items._cn_summary: LISKER是1979年巴斯克地区的前卫民谣乐队，来自西班牙东北部埃ibor，由原Jeki乐队的民谣乐手和Zima乐队的迷幻摇滚乐手合并而成。乐队受Cream、Hendrix、King Crimson等西方摇滚影响，但将巴斯克民谣旋律与迷幻吉他噪音相融合，呈现出独特的声音。专辑五首曲目约35分钟，长笛占据主导地位，类似Jethro Tull的风格，但以粗粝的模糊吉他取代理性键盘编排，形成无 symphonic 的空灵气质。作品以器乐为主，巴斯克语演唱穿插其中，从开篇的民谣摇滚渐进至终曲的九分钟长篇《Eldarniotik iheska》，展示渐进式摇滚的结构张力。作为巴斯克地下乐坛的非主流作品，其跨文化融合与地区独特性值得肯定。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The presence of Jim Pembroke and Jukka Gustavson didn't guarantee the Wigwam we all remember, and their debut is divided into two parts. The first is anchored in that 60s swing, with a groove-laden jazz-blues sound, where, nevertheless, glimpses of the highly personal compositional style that years later would lead them to their masterpieces alongside Pekka Pohjola can be seen. This is especially true in tracks like "En Aio Paeta," because in others like "Guardian Angel / The Future," the influence of Steve Wingwood is still noticeable.However, one can enjoy the unique approach to jazz, with its distinctive Finnish flavor, and Wiggam wouldn't lose that even in his more progressive and personal period. "No Pens, El Karsinoita," with its piano and Ronnie �sterberg's drums, perfectly captures that particular mood.The second part of Hard N' Horny, a concept album dedicated to a middle-aged man named Henry. Otto Donner's string arrangements suit it perfectly, and despite remaining anchored in that jazzy freshness of the '60s...as in Henry's...Mountain Range or Thereabouts, a kind of timeless limbo surrounds it, which vibraphones, or the Rolling Stones-style psychedelia of Ghastly and Diabolical Mistakes, propels in other directions.Ears, Eyes, Girlfriends and Feet achieves the desired atmosphere for Henry's conceptual work, but we don't find that special alchemy found in Fairyport or Being.A kind of Charleston in the Kinks style in Hard and Horny All-Niter, however, ends up being more homogeneous than its predecessor, Tombstone Valentine, showcasing the burgeoning talent of two of Wigwam's creative minds...waiting for the third.
items._cn_summary: WIGWAM发行于1969年的首张专辑Hard N' Horny属于早期芬兰爵士摇滚/融合作品，专辑分两部分：第一部分延续60年代摇摆风格，以爵士蓝调为基调，融入芬兰本土特色；第二部分为献给中年男子Henry的概念专辑，采用Otto Donner的弦乐编排。评论指出专辑具有vibraphones与Rolling Stones式迷幻元素，展现了该乐团独特的芬兰爵士风味。作为60年代末的前卫融合尝试，专辑体现了早期实验精神与芬兰文化视角的结合，虽未达到后来 Fairyport 与 Being 的高度，但对了解Wigwam音乐发展脉络具有一定参考价值。

items.body: You took my hand and took my painThis kind of chance, it has no nameInto the nightThe shadows become truth Corlyx’s Sweeter Than Blood, the first single from the band’s forthcoming twelve-track record, takes vampire romance seriously, though not so seriously that one cannot hear a faint bat-wing rustle of theatrical pleasure. The song lives in the Gothic bargain between appetite and devotion, where the lover may be rescuer, risk, or both. Its title suggests intimacy as a force stronger than hunger, which is a useful proposition for anyone trying to date a mysterious count from the ‘Old Country.’ Guitars cut cleanly through the mix, the drums give the track a firmer physical spine, and Caitlin Stokes sings as though desire has led her into a room where every promise arrives with paperwork and possibly a puncture wound. The release marks another turn in Corlyx’s ongoing transformation. What began as a darkwave duo has grown through a post-punk trio phase into a full-band lineup, now sharpened by the arrival of British drummer Flow Toulman. The result, by the band’s own account, leans toward an alternative rock-meets-classic 80s post-punk synthesis, with goth and deathrock moving to the forefront, while the electronic club DNA remains alive beneath the surface. One can hear kinship with Strange Boutique, The March Violets, Octavian Winters, Feyleux, and Anne Bennett, though Corlyx’s current approach has more bite than polish. There are fangs in the catchy-as-hell hook, but thankfully, no one is making a meal of it. “This song was inspired by Dracula’s deep enchantment for his beloved Mina, how his love was sweeter than his bloodlust,” says Stokes. “I drew parallels from this idea with my own life experiences in having walls up, guarding my heart, and finally meeting the person who showed me what love could be.” Sweeter Than Blood follows a nocturnal encounter in which love feels restorative and suspect at once. A cold pull leads the speaker away from ordinary daylight and toward someone who can remove pain, offer protection, and possibly open a wound of another kind. Romance is a threshold: one person stepping toward another while still remembering what abandonment taught them. The heart may be guarded, but the lock has begun to crumble into love dust. Stokes has also framed Corlyx’s new material as part of a broader return to instruments, bodies, and visible musicianship. “Bands more than ever now need to separate from machines, the listener needs to know right away that a human musician(S) made the song,” Stokes insists. “Just another puzzle piece that pushed us in this direction, but in a subconscious way, it certainly wasn’t deliberate when we started making this next record. It just sort of turned out this way naturally.” Brandon Ashley describes the shift in similarly practical terms. “We started writing the demos for our next album by having our new drummer track first, this brought a lot new energy, and the guitar sounds we normally use needed more variety,” he explains. “We still have all our classic post-punk sounds, some of them being very unique to us, but as the songs developed we realised things were sounding altogether more Rock.” The video, directed and edited by Stokes, extends that transformation into image. She also handled the set design and band styling, hand-making many parts of the outfits, with Jason Kahl partially shooting the clip. In it, Stokes appears in a striking white vampire cape, wandering through halls with goblets, severe glances, and ceremonial poise. Around the band performance, the imagery suggests old blood, guarded hearts, and the glamour of surrender. Corlyx enters its next era with a song that treats love as fever, a bargain, and a cure…with just enough fang to leave an imprint in the skin. Watch the video for Sweeter Than Blood below: Listen to Sweeter Than Blood below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: Corlyx是一支来自欧美的Goth Rock乐队，《Sweeter Than Blood》为其即将发行的十二首曲目专辑的首支单曲。音乐风格融合了经典80年代post-punk、暗潮（darkwave）与deathrock元素，同时保留了一定的电子底色，属于用户关注的核心音乐类型。歌词以Dracula与Mina的吸血鬼浪漫为灵感，探讨欲望、痛苦与脆弱情感之间的张力。Caitlin Stokes的演唱带有文学性与戏剧张力。乐队从darkwave双人组合发展到完整编制，新加入的英国鼓手Flow Toulman为作品带来更具物理感的节奏骨架。编曲上吉他与鼓点清晰突出，兼具alternative rock的力量感与暗潮音乐的冷冽气质。歌词的文学性引用与乐队近年强调现场乐器演奏、回归人体音乐性的理念为作品增色，是暗潮与后朋克领域内风格扎实、有所融合的独立制作。

items.body: In a world of constant illusion Society is wired in A hive mind controls what we want Losing ourselves from within On Ghosts, Sheffield’s IAMIMPERFECT write as though the mid-2020s have become a pressure system inside the skull: everything hums, everything tightens, and every private injury has somehow learned to speak in public. The title is apt, though these apparitions belong less to candlelit folklore than to modern fatigue. They haunt us with the need to pass among one’s peers, the ache of comparison, the competitor always gaining ground, the plain cruelty of seeing everyone else appear to cope while your own life keeps tilting off its axis. The band’s music sits at the junction of darkwave, synth-pop, industrial, and goth, with electronic drums snapping under intricate synth arrangements, distorted guitar adding a metallic ache, and vocal hooks that rise with a theatrical insistence. The reference points are clear enough: Solar Fake, The Birthday Massacre, Faderhead, Depeche Mode, with a stray Iron Maiden flourish cutting through the machinery – but IAMIMPERFECT are most persuasive when those ingredients serve emotional consequence rather than genre inventory. Surviving Is Not Living sets the album’s moral temperature, with its cinematic synth sighs. Its vocals lay bare the central wound of imbalance: one person takes, the other keeps giving; one person seems required, the other feels merely tolerated. The anger is sharpened by exhaustion, but the track’s real force comes from its refusal to accept humiliation as fate. With its driving melody, The Fallen widens the frame from private injury to civic collapse, picturing society as a wired collective where freedom and control blur until people become strangers to themselves. It is one of the record’s stronger pieces, bleak without becoming vague. Conversion Therapy, with its mechanized beat, is the most explicit and severe track here, treating abuse disguised as salvation with appropriate disgust. The language of poison, brainwashing, exploitation, and PTSD is direct because the subject allows no polite softening. In the dirgeful, rhythmic lament Solitary Shell, shame and religious judgment curdle into isolation, but the song keeps searching for will, drive, and some stubborn remnant of connection. The final track, Ghosts Of The Past, with its bright, wistful synth melody, somber vocal, and zig-zag guitar riff, closes the circle with abandonment and the cruel arithmetic of unanswered messages. Ghosts is available on all major digital platforms worldwide. Listen to Ghosts below and order the EP here. Ghosts by IAmImperfect Formed in Sheffield in late 2023, the project moved quickly through UK gigs, festival appearances, the 2024 Reincarnate EP, and a 2025 stretch that included a southern England tour. That pace gives Ghosts a charged, breathless quality, as though the songs were written in the narrow gap between damage and decision. The EP’s artwork deepens the album’s emotional architecture. Working with Sheffield artists Stephen Carley and Scott D’arcy, IAMIMPERFECT turned double-exposed film photographs into visual companions for each track, giving the record a carefully distressed frame. Ghosts is about trying to live while the world claws at your attention, pulls you toward conformity, and drags you back toward despair. More crucially, it is about continuing anyway. Follow IAMIMPERFECT: Spotify Facebook Instagram Bandcamp The post “In a World of Constant Illusion” — Sheffield Dark Synth Duo IAMIMPERFECT Share Haunting “Ghosts” EP appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 英国谢菲尔德暗潮电子双人组合IAMIMPERFECT的最新EP《Ghosts》，融合darkwave、synth-pop、industrial与goth元素，以电子鼓、精密合成器编排与失真吉他构建冷冽阴暗的音景。歌词聚焦现代社会中群体压力与个体失衡，探讨社会压迫与个人情感创伤的共鸣。乐队将经典暗潮参照如Depeche Mode、Solar Fake与Faderhead与Iron Maiden吉他风味相融合，在类型传统中注入批判深度与情感内核。整体作品情感表达尖锐而不失厚重，曲式工整且具实验气质，是近期英国暗潮场景中值得关注的新声。

items.body: Brussels’ Unfathomless label returns with a pair of complementary releases, each a single album-length work. Tossapol imagines two museums, one real and one imaginary, while Ludovic Medery walks through the Colonster Woods, gathering sonic impressions. These are the 94th and 95th releases on the imprint as they approach their celebratory centennial. When Tossapol was a child, a new science museum was built nearby: shiny and filled with promise. The planetarium alone was a source of wonder. Now the “exhibits are not as new as they were before,” the lights are dim and the newness is diminished. The artist’s return prompts reflection on an “imaginary building” constructed from memory and impression. These two museums are now conflated. The piece begins with the welcoming sounds of door chimes, morning birds and passing traffic. For many, an initial visit to the science museum was a school trip, wide-open doors discharging hoards of excited children. Time may either shine or dull the memories; this artist highlights the abrasion. Instead of sight, the museum becomes a location of sound: rustling wind and creaking corridors. One imagines attendance is not as it once was. In the eighth minute, one can hear a single person fumbling around, wondering where everyone has gone, whistling and tapping. Light conversation in the tenth minute offers assurance that the real museum still possesses some allure. But what of the imaginary museum? To listen is to wonder at the sound of each subsequent exhibit: trickling water, tour guides, and rubbery, balloon-like utterances. The real museum is now a museum of feelings: this is how I felt then, this is how I feel now. sédiment is by nature a more bucolic recording, again translating visual impressions into sound: as Ludovic Medery puts it, “sound filming.” The challenge is like describing light to a blind man, but one knows it can be done: music contains light and dark passages, and so do the woods. In the opening minutes, Medery finds delight in the resonance of a metal drum, perhaps deserted in the riverside. There is crackle here, and rustle, and flow; might one also call it a museum? The sonic appeal of a forest is found not only in the expected sounds, but in the unexpected and unexplained, the latter which may cause a momentary frisson: am I safe in these woods? One begins to hear animals, or something worse, while surrendering to the imagination. A roaring stream restores the balance, a sonic irony in that water sounds are soothing, but do not necessarily mean that one is safe. Hammering home this point, a plane flies dangerously low and disturbs the reverie. Twigs snap; or is Medery doing the snapping? But by the halfway point, the piece settles into a rhythm, including a natural tempo, including percussive pops. The feelings of the listener shift, as they likely do for the artist. A local resident ~ frog, bird, bug? ~ provides high-pitched commentary, like a squeaky toy. At the end, thunder frightens, but rain refuses to fall. These artists do more than record sound: they convey the feelings connected to such sound. The museum isn’t just a museum; the forest isn’t just a forest. To experience both is to wonder at the difference between sounds heard, meanings imagined and value imbued. (Richard Allen)
items._cn_summary: 两张专辑均来自比利时独立厂牌Unfathomless，展现了声音艺术与实验音乐的深度探索。Tossapol的《two museums》通过博物馆记忆与声音的交织，将童年经历与现实参观转化为沉浸式的声景体验，强调听觉而非视觉。Ludovic Medery的《sédiment》则采用“声音拍摄”概念，以森林实地录音为基础，融入想象性元素，通过金属鼓、流水、动物声响构建自然音景。两张作品都具有强烈的概念性和实验性，将field recording、声音记忆与想象空间相融合，属于当代实验音乐范畴。专辑定位小众，适合对声音艺术和实验音乐有深入兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by Finnforest — A Most Welcome Reprieve Stumbling half-conscious through the wreckage of mid-80s Banco, one could be forgiven for despairwhile pondering what could possibly follow E Via, the 1985 album that many figured must bethe end of the progressive juggernaut, for real this time. After all, it made 90125 andGenesis Shapes seem like masterpiece-level material by comparison. E Via had hit melike the worst moments of Chicago 17 and Invisible Touch put through a blender. I felt ready to liedown and embrace the end when, out of absolute nowhere, arrives Donna Plautilla. I don't know who Donna is supposed to be historically, but to me she was an angel of mercy in thismoment of Banco's discog. While dropping in 1989, the archival material was actually recorded 20years earlier by the newly-formed Banco of the late '60s: the Nocenzi brothers, the Falco brothers,and Franco Pontecorvi. This is embryonic Banco music and, despite falling well short of the grandeurof their acclaimed 72-73 albums, it is nonetheless absolutely enjoyable proto-prog in the same veinas the first Yes album, From Genesis to Revelation, Ad Gloriam, and '60s Deep Purple.Yes, it is dated now and has a little bit of that '60s Iron Butterfly psych vibe and short songsformat that place it well short of something like Darwin, but even without Francesco DiGiacomo's vocal talent, one can still hear the beginnings of what might follow. The album is wellrecorded and mixed, so it sounds pretty fab considering the age and, at that point, unknown statureof the group. The tracks here are keyboard-led period rock that is slightly less adventurous than, say, the Yesdebut, but only slightly, and it quite nicely preludes the RPI movement that was soon coming.Without Di Giacomo in the fold at this point, the vocals are handled by Vittorio Nocenzi, and whilehe lacks the legendary Di Giacomo's pipes, the fact is that he does just fine. He's no slouch as asinger, and he has backing from the Falco brothers (who were from the band Crash). As you mightimagine, the songs have that certain Italian spice that informs the music, from the beautifullanguage to the all-too-brief classical guitar and flute and harpsichord moments. Otherwise thesongs are driven by great piano and organ runs backed by upbeat, grooving rhythm section. I love thebold and up-front bass by Fabrizio Falco. The songs may indeed be proto-prog, but they are neverboring or lacking enthusiasm. The tunes are engaging and well composed and not as dated in the "flowery sense" as otherpeer '60s "organ rock." Is this album going to change your world? Likely not, but it is a really nice gem for the Banco fangenerally, the chance to hear them in this developing stage and with good audio quality. Perhaps mypraise of this album is partially the result of being bludgeoned into near catatonic haze by EVia, with Donna by contrast coming across as some kind of manna from heaven due to myE Via waterboarding. I can't say. But I had a good time with Donna, whoever she was. Ihighly recommend this early glimpse of RPI for the sheer joy of the playing and obvious burgeoningcreativity. It's slam dunk 3 stars, and I'm right on the edge of going 4.
items._cn_summary: 意大利前卫摇滚乐团Banco del Mutuo Soccorso的《Donna Plautilla》录制于1960年代末，但直到1989年才发行。专辑展现了乐团早期发展阶段的音乐雏形，融合了古典吉他、长笛、羽管键琴等古典元素与键盘主导的摇滚架构，带有明显的意大利文化特色。风格上接近早期Yes和60年代Deep Purple，属于proto-prog范畴，歌曲结构相对简短但编排精致。作为小众独立发行的复古作品，专辑录音质量上佳，展示了乐团从实验探索到成熟风格的演变过程。对于关注实验与前卫音乐的用户而言，该专辑提供了了解意大利RPI运动源头的有价值窗口，融合古典与摇滚的尝试也具有一定跨领域价值。
